messages:
Maya: Heads-up 1: AcmeCare wants more than a usage carveout. Their procurement emailed: they need an SLA floor for POC availability, a limited liability cap for trial period only, and audit access to logs for troubleshooting. They won't sign without that.
Luis: Oof. SLA for a POC is unusual but doable if we keep it scoped (e.g., 99% availability during business hours for the POC window). We should prefer an Order Form Appendix not touching the MSA core liability.
Grace: From product: we can commit to a scoped uptime measurement (region X) and provide logs for debugging. Full audit access (raw logs) is product-restricted; we can offer aggregated telemetry + redacted logs.
Ethan: Finance note: liability caps are risky. For POC we can do a time-boxed liability cap equal to fees paid for the POC or a fixed dollar cap (e.g., $10k). That keeps it finite and accepted by RevOps.
Maya: Draft language idea (order form appendix):
```
POC Appendix (Order Form)
1) POC Term: 45 days from Effective Date.
2) Availability: Provider will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain 99% availability during 9am-6pm PT for the POC region. Availability measured via Provider's health checks; credits only for downtime > 30m in aggregate.
3) Limited Liability (POC only): Notwithstanding anything in the MSA, Provider's aggregate liability for claims arising solely from the POC shall be limited to the total fees paid for the POC or $10,000, whichever is less.
4) Logs & Audit: Provider will deliver aggregated telemetry and redacted request logs upon Customer request for troubleshooting. Raw sensitive logs are excluded unless mutually agreed via an engineering runbook.
5) Billing Activation: Customer must submit PO number within 7 calendar days of signature; otherwise billing activation will be delayed until PO receipt.
6) No POC auto-renewal.
```
Luis: That should address procurement. We also need an ops gating line: "Provider may enforce rate limits or throttle non-critical traffic if usage exceeds agreed thresholds; Provider will notify Customer prior to throttling."
DevOpsBot: infra note: Can implement throttles and availability monitoring. Need token/day profile + preferred region. Please provide by EOD.
Grace: On logs: we can produce a redaction template and an access checklist for audit requests. That tends to keep legal comfortable without product changes.
LegalBot: Suggestion: keep the MSA untouched; add the Appendix and a single-line DPA addendum pointing to our SOC2 and encryption at rest, plus an optional KMS integration statement (subject to ops enablement).
Ethan: Also confirm payment terms: net30 standard, but procurement asked net60. Finance will accept net60 only if PO issued at signing and deal desk approves. Otherwise stick to net30 + PO confirmation.
Maya: Signature routing ask: they want Exec Legal (acme.legal@redacted) to sign the Order Form and require Procurement (purchasing@acmecare.com) to acknowledge the PO number before activation. Can we route esign accordingly?
Luis: Yes. Our esign supports signer, cc, and acknowledgement steps. We'll route sign to Exec Legal, cc Procurement + Billing, and set a required form field for "PO number" that must be filled within 7 days.
Maya: OK. I'll prepare the Appendix + DPA addendum drafts and post them here. If legal/ops agree, I'll send two variants: (A) $10k fixed cap, (B) cap = POC fees paid.
Grace: Ops: once we get token/day profile, we'll set throttles and confirm region-level uptime monitoring config.
Ethan: I'll flag net60 to RevOps for pre-approval but expect a delay. If they insist on net60, we should ask for a signed PO upfront.
Maya: Thanks. tagging @DevOpsBot and @LegalBot. Will post draft in ~2 hours. :wave:
